extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (also shared with the public)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners applying the 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance (2019 PEG) to determine whether claims satisfy 35 U.S.C. § 101 (judicial exceptions, practical application, and inventive concept). Focused on examination procedure, drafting Office actions, and handling pending prosecutions and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2019 PEG became effective as of its publication on January 7, 2019 and should be implemented immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All patent examiners (except those in TC 2900) will be trained; information and training materials are posted to the external website and the 101 microsite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall eligibility framework unchanged
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2019 PEG does not change the overall subject matter eligibility two-step framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1 (statutory categories), the streamlined analysis, and Step 2B remain unchanged; only Step 2A procedure is revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised Step 2A two-prong inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Under revised Step 2A a claim is eligible unless: (1) it recites a judicial exception; and (2) the exception is not integrated into a practical application of the exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-prong inquiry replaces prior Step 2A procedure. Examiners must identify judicial exceptions and then evaluate integration into a practical application (Prong 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated groupings of abstract ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract idea exception includes the following groupings: mathematical concepts, certain methods of organizing human activity, and mental processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are to use these enumerated groupings to identify abstract ideas and are no longer to use the prior 'Eligibility Quick Reference Sheet Identifying Abstract Ideas' (Abstract Idea QRS). If a limitation is treated as an abstract idea but not within these groupings, Director approval is required (rare).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of BRI to determine abstraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the broadest reasonable interpretation (BRI) of the claim in view of the specification to decide if the claim limitation falls within an enumerated grouping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If at least one embodiment within the BRI of the limitation(s), when viewed in context of the claim as a whole, falls within an enumerated grouping, then the claim recites an abstract idea and requires further analysis at Step 2A Prong Two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on examples as basis for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim concepts should not be compared to prior §101 examples to determine abstract idea status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare claimed concepts to the enumerated groupings in the 2019 PEG instead. Examples may illustrate application of groupings for particular fact situations but should not be required models for applicants. Use new Examples 37–42 to understand 2019 PEG application; exercise caution with Examples 1–36.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'integration into a practical application' (Step 2A Prong Two)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration requires additional element(s) (or combination) to apply, rely on, or use the judicial exception in a manner that imposes a meaningful limit on the exception so the claim is more than a drafting effort designed to monopolize the exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify additional elements beyond the judicial exception and evaluate whether those elements meaningfully limit the exception. This is a new analytical step not found in prior guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between Step 2A Prong Two and Step 2B
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 2A Prong Two evaluates whether additional elements integrate the exception into a practical application but does not consider whether those elements are well-understood, routine, conventional activity; Step 2B evaluates inventive concept including conventionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Prong Two omits the conventionality check, claims with conventional elements can nonetheless integrate an exception at Prong Two. Step 2B must be applied where appropriate to assess 'significantly more.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement-to-technology analysis at Step 2A
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering whether a claim pertains to an improvement to the functioning of a computer or other technology, analyze the improvement without reference to whether the elements are well-understood, routine, conventional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MPEP 2106.04(a) and 2106.05(a) for discussion of improvements insofar as they do not contradict the 2019 PEG; the analysis focuses on whether the claim pertains to a technological improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventional elements can integrate an exception
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional element that is well-understood, routine, conventional activity can nonetheless integrate a judicial exception into a practical application in Step 2A Prong Two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Prong Two consider all additional elements — conventional or not — when evaluating integration into a practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2B (inventive concept / 'significantly more') requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 2B analysis (inventive concept) is unchanged and evaluates whether claimed elements add significantly more than the judicial exception, including assessing whether elements are well-understood, routine, conventional activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an examiner asserts that an element (or combination) is well-understood, routine, conventional activity, the examiner must support that assertion with evidence consistent with the Berkheimer memo (use one of memo options 1–4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reevaluation when Prong Two finds insignificant extra-solution activity
rubrics_metrics.description: If Step 2A Prong Two concludes an additional element is insignificant extra-solution activity, the claim must be reevaluated under Step 2B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Step 2B finds the element unconventional or otherwise more than routine, that may indicate an inventive concept and render the claim eligible. Other Step 2B considerations may not need reevaluation if the answer will be the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling applications previously rejected under prior guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When next acting on applications with pre-2019 PEG §101 rejections, the examiner must analyze claims under the 2019 PEG and withdraw prior rejections where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdraw prior §101 rejection if the examiner determines the claim does not recite a judicial exception, integrates the exception into a practical application, or provides an inventive concept. A §101 rejection may be made final only if the basic thrust of the rejection remains the same as in the previous Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a change constitutes a new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A new ground of rejection exists when a rejection relies upon new facts or a new rationale not previously raised to the applicant; certain changes do not constitute a new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not new grounds: maintaining that claim recites an abstract idea but changing explanation to refer to enumerated groupings; relying on same Step 2B considerations; changing form paragraphs. If basic thrust is changed, prosecution must be reopened and next action cannot be final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tentative abstract ideas require Director approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner determines a limitation does not fall within enumerated groupings but still believes it is an abstract idea (a 'tentative abstract idea'), Technology Center Director approval is required before mailing a rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This situation should be rare; follow the procedure in the 2019 PEG for tentative abstract ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant requests for supplemental Office action procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant requests supplemental action after publication of the 2019 PEG arguing prior §101 rejection does not comply with new guidance, applicant should file a written response pointing out errors per 37 CFR 1.111(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews may be conducted to clarify issues (MPEP 713) but examiners should not issue new Office actions solely in response to oral requests; all business should be transacted in writing (37 CFR 1.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action explanation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a §101 rejection the Office action must provide an explanation why each claim is patent ineligible that is sufficiently clear and specific to provide applicant notice and enable an effective response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For abstract ideas, explain which specific limitation(s) correspond to an enumerated grouping or justify why a limitation is treated as an abstract idea if it does not fall within the enumerated groupings (rare and requires Director approval). Also explain why the claim does not integrate the judicial exception into a practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: New and superseded form paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.05.015 is superseded and should no longer be used. Use existing 7.04.01, 7.05 and new form paragraphs for Step 2B rejections and specified situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the recited judicial exception is an abstract idea enumerated in the 2019 PEG, use new form paragraph 7.05.016. If the abstract idea is not enumerated, use 7.05.016 and new 7.05.017 and obtain Director approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifying the record when withdrawing a prior rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If withdrawing a prior §101 rejection under the 2019 PEG, it is helpful for the examiner to briefly explain on the record why the rejection is withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying remarks may be made at any point during prosecution including with a notice of allowance; see MPEP 2106.07(c) for guidance on clarifying the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing court decisions consistently with PEG
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may cite court decisions to support identification of claimed subject matter as an abstract idea, but the identification must be consistent with the 2019 PEG and its enumerated groupings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address applicant's arguments regarding specific cases similarly to how examiners address case-based arguments in other patentability grounds. Indicating the appropriate grouping(s) for a previously-identified abstract idea does not change the basic thrust of the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals handling discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Notice of Appeal was filed and final rejection included §101 grounds, the Technology Center may choose to reopen prosecution or to designate a new ground of rejection in the examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should confer with their SPE if aware of applications on appeal that may be affected. See MPEP 1207.03 for guidance on new grounds of rejection in an examiner's answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued updating of SME court decision chart
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chart of Subject Matter Eligibility (SME) Court decisions will continue to be updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may consult the chart as it is maintained and updated by the Office to track case law relevant to subject matter eligibility.
